# SimJury complete public-site guide

This document describes every canonical public page and every phase of the interactive SimJury experience without disclosing case answers or case-specific facts.

## Product

SimJury's Daily Docket is a static-first exercise in judgment. Each sitting presents one serious criminal case in a contemporary courtroom. The player occupies Juror 01's seat, hears both sides, and tests the evidence with an authored eleven-juror room. When the availability-gated live-jury beta is open, invited people can deliberate in the same room alongside the clearly labelled authored jurors. After about twenty minutes, the player may record Guilty, Not Guilty, or Undecided / No verdict. Any juror may remain undecided, and the room can return a unanimous verdict, majority verdict, or hung jury with no verdict.

There are no public accounts, public leaderboards, or runtime generative AI. Solo play remains local. Optional private live rooms use short-lived room state only for invited human participants.

## Canonical public routes

### https://simjury.com/

The static home page explains the value proposition, mature-content scope, approximate duration, local save model, and three-part journey: hear both sides, deliberate from the evidence, then lock a verdict. Its primary action opens the Daily Docket.

### https://simjury.com/today/

The Daily Docket is an interactive JavaScript application. Its raw HTML contains a readable fallback summary for clients that do not execute JavaScript. The complete player journey is:

1. First visit: accept a guided introductory sitting or skip directly to today's case.
2. Case selection: open today's featured sitting or any case in the browser-side seven-case library, including the guided introduction.
3. Briefing: read the title, charge, case-specific advisory, accused's position, and instructions.
4. Openings: hear the prosecution and defence frame the dispute.
5. Evidence: move through each authored evidence beat in order, read or listen, and write private notes.
6. Closings: hear both advocates draw their arguments together.
7. Deliberation: choose evidence, ask questions, and raise original concerns across three rounds while authored jurors respond. If the live-jury beta is available, invited humans can exchange messages and stated positions in the same transcript alongside clearly labelled authored replies. Seat leanings and tallies remain hidden.
8. Individual view and jury result: record Guilty, Not Guilty, or Undecided / No verdict after deliberation. The player, authored jurors, and human jurors may remain undecided; the room can agree unanimously, reach the jurisdiction's permitted majority, or return no verdict because it is hung.
9. Judgment and reveal: hear the room's unanimous, majority, or hung result; compare it with the player's view; inspect the case analysis and reveal; update local statistics; and optionally create a spoiler-safe share card.

Narration is optional. Authored audio is fetched as static media when available, with browser speech as a fallback. The app supports keyboard navigation, visible focus, semantic headings, transcript text alongside audio, responsive desktop and mobile layouts, and reduced-motion preferences.

The case library is a chooser inside `/today/`, not a collection of separate case URLs. These crawl guides therefore do not reproduce or link case answers or case-specific facts.

### https://simjury.com/privacy/

The static privacy page explains:

- progress, notes, verdicts, narration preferences, and sitting statistics are stored in the current browser;
- there is no cross-browser or cross-device sync, account recovery, or backend player-state service;
- clearing site data or changing browser/profile/device removes access to those local records;
- optional narration requests public audio clips from GitHub Releases, so GitHub can observe ordinary request metadata, timing, and opaque clip identifiers;
- Cloudflare receives ordinary request metadata while delivering the static site;
- SimJury adds no analytics or tracking code;
- cases and juror responses are pre-authored, with deterministic outcomes computed locally and no runtime generative AI.

## Discovery and HTTP behavior

- `https://simjury.com/robots.txt` permits all user agents and names the XML sitemap.
- `https://simjury.com/sitemap.xml` lists every canonical public HTML page.
- `https://simjury.com/llms.txt` provides the concise machine-readable index.
- Unknown routes return a real HTTP 404 page.
- `/play/` redirects to `/today/`.
- `/install/` redirects to `/`; the former app and installer were removed.

## Architecture and cost boundary

GitHub-authored site and solo-case assets deploy through Cloudflare Static Assets and bypass compute. Only `/api/live/*`, `/api/waitlist` and `/discord/interactions` invoke a bounded Worker. Live-jury coordination and short-lived room state use three SQLite Durable Objects; the optional email waitlist uses a single D1 database holding addresses, the consent wording and date, and a daily keyed fingerprint used only to limit signups per source. The service uses no KV, R2, Queues, runtime AI, analytics, or dynamic rendering. Case text and the deterministic deliberation engine remain bundled at build time. This guide is served identically to browsers and crawlers; there is no user-agent branching or bot-only content.

## Spoiler and publication boundary

This crawl guide intentionally excludes verdict truth, twists, trap analysis, exact juror rules, hidden tallies, and case-specific titles and facts. The interactive app's static bundle contains its complete pre-authored seven-case library, but this guide neither reproduces nor links those details, so ordinary crawl discovery does not spoil a sitting.
